q: What was the head of the great image made of?
why: “Thou art this head of gold.” Daniel tells Nebuchadnezzar that his kingdom is the head.

q: Which kingdom does Daniel 2 name outright?
why: Only the head is named in the chapter: Nebuchadnezzar’s Babylon. The later kingdoms are named in Daniel 8 or identified from history.

q: In Daniel 8, who are the ram with two horns and the rough goat?
why: “The ram … are the kings of Media and Persia. And the rough goat is the king of Grecia.”

q: What were the feet of the image made of?
why: “His feet part of iron and part of clay.” A divided kingdom, partly strong and partly broken.

q: What struck the image on its feet?
a: A stone cut out without hands
why: “A stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet.”

a: A great mountain that filled the whole earth
why: It is the kingdom that the God of heaven sets up, which “shall never be destroyed.”

q: Which king did some critics once call a fiction, until a cylinder from Ur named him?
why: The Nabonidus Cylinders, found at Ur in 1854, name Belshazzar as Nabonidus’s eldest son.

q: According to the Nabonidus Chronicle, how did Babylon fall in 539 BC?
a: Cyrus’s army entered without a battle
It was destroyed by an earthquake
why: The chronicle says the army of Cyrus “entered Babylon without battle.” Daniel 5 says the kingdom fell that very night.

q: Which beast of Daniel 7 had four wings and four heads?
why: “Like a leopard, which had upon the back of it four wings of a fowl; the beast had also four heads.”

q: Where did Alexander the Great die in 323 BC?
why: “When he was strong, the great horn was broken.” He died in Babylon, and four kingdoms arose from his empire.

q: Who were thrown into the fiery furnace?
why: They would not bow to the golden image, and a fourth figure was seen with them in the fire.

q: Which event of AD 70 matches Daniel 9:26?
a: Rome destroyed Jerusalem and its temple
Rome split into east and west
why: “The people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary.” The Arch of Titus still shows the spoils.
